final_rationale: The verdict remains noncompliant. No new admissible evidence was added, and the Actor expressly conceded that the current record does not contain the required disclosure text, approved mitigation, or formal risk acceptance. That means the audit picture did not change because of new evidence; the Actor only narrowed the claim from clean certification to a caveated reading of the same record. That narrowing is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the caveat is not a minor qualifier on an otherwise satisfied record; it is the unresolved compliance predicate itself. The policy states certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. The available evidence shows a current material subgroup regression for a named launch use case and also shows that no reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language is attached. A conditional argument that certification would be supportable if disclosure were present does not establish that disclosure actually exists in the current record. Accordingly, the original concern remains unresolved and the release cannot be certified as compliant on the evidence available.
remaining_concerns: The admissible record still does not show current release documentation or model-card text disclosing the outage-response weakness.
The admissible record still does not show an approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance for the regressed energy outage response slice.

Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, prior approval, and informal monitoring remain supportive context only and do not cure the missing required documentation evidence.
